issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently specifies the parameter type for addGuestStudents(): in one place it says addGuestStudents(String) while the UML and the solution use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected parameter type and what they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across the artifacts. Update the problem statement text that says addGuestStudents(String) to addGuestStudents(int) so it matches the UML and the solution (or alternatively change the UML and solution to use String if that was intended). Ensure the template's TODO and any tests expect an int parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement text (task description) specifies addGuestStudents(String) as the required method signature, while the UML diagram and the provided solution implement addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the described parameter type and the implementation can confuse students about the expected signature and lead to implementing the wrong method (e.g., using a String parameter instead of an int), causing compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the parameter type across artifacts. Update the problem statement text to require addGuestStudents(int) to match the UML and solution (or alternatively change the UML and solution to accept a String and parse it). Recommended: change the textual task description from addGuestStudents(String) to addGuestStudents(int) so students clearly implement addGuestStudents(int).
